subject: Reporting Factor Correlations instead of Covariance

messages.author: c1e1212cf2e076c1
messages.subject: Reporting Factor Correlations instead of Covariance
parts:
Is there a way you can specify the model to report out the correlations between factor/latent variables instead of their covariance? I'm running models with categorical and binary manifest variables.

Thanks

Robin

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Reporting Factor Correlations instead of Covariance
parts:
On 10/26/2013 03:47 AM, robin ghertner wrote:
> Is there a way you can specify the model to report out the correlations
> between factor/latent variables instead of their covariance? I'm running
> models with categorical and binary manifest variables.

Are your referring to the covariances reported in the summary() output?
In this case, using the standardized=TRUE argument as in

summary(fit, standardized=TRUE)

will give you correlactions in the Std.lv and Std.all columns.

If you need the model-implied correlations among the latents, you can use

inspect(fit, "cor.lv")

If all latents are exogenous, this will give the same information. But
this is not true in general.

Yves.
